NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 825 9376 8651, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 825 9376 8651, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 10, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:02 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Jacob Parker and Will Deley of Los Hermanos led the flag salute.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING NOVEMBER 28, 2020 AS "SMALL BUSINESS
  SATURDAY"

B.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF
  FREE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE - FOURTH
  QUARTER 2020

Sharon Shapiro-Fox of Waste Management drew names for the 4th quarter winners to receive
one free year of service:

  FOURTH QUARTER RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 15 Cresta Verdes Drive
  FOURTH QUARTER COMMERCIAL WINNER: Merrill Gardens of RHE

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF OCTOBER & NOVEMBER 2020

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 10, 2020
   APPROVED WARRANTS 63316 THROUGH 63346 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $349,021.71 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100620 THROUGH
  100720; 63303, 63163 VOID; IN THE AMOUNT OF $79,768.45 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $428,790.16 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 20, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 26, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 27, 2020

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Rhys Moon from Peninsula High School provided information about his website
MindfulCoping.net, dedicated to sharing valuable strategies and personal insight to those
with mental illness.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE LOCAL APPOINTMENT  LIST  AND
  APPOINTMENT PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL noted that Dan Porter on the Equestrian Committee may
have moved and his residence should be confirmed before possible reappointment.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested that original appointment dates for Commission and
Committee Members be added as a column on the Local Appointment List.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  FIRST QUARTER BUDGET REVIEW FY 2020-21

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL requested an update for PV Transit funding with schools still
not in session. Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained that they are being
funded, and stated that the City has been billed for the first installment.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF asked how line item #3630 (PWEC Concessionaire's Fee) on page
6 in Exhibit A related to line item #3450 (Stable Rental & Concessionaire Enterprise Funds).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 10, 2020
 Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained that item line item #3450 is the
remaining balance from the Stables Enterprise Fund that was carried over from FY16-17.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN requested an update on the Anastasi project near the post
office, in which Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba stated they were
likely still approximately 18 months from completion.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN inquired about sales tax from online purchases made from
within the City, which Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained goes into a County
Pool in which the City receive a portion of. Discussion ensued regarding how the County Sales
Tax Pool works and how the numbers are reported, which Director Whitehead stated would be
further discussed at next year’s Policy Development Session.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained the Fund Balance Policy line item for
Hawthorne Canyon, noting it is a legal requirement, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM
ZUCKERMAN.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PROPOSAL FOR PROFESSIONAL PLANNING SERVICES FOR DEVELOPMENT
  OF AN ADU PROGRAM AS PART OF THE SB 2 GRANT AWARD

Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL inquired if ADUs would be counted towards the City’s
affordable housing allocation. Planning Manager Naughton explained that without a deed
restriction being recorded on a property, any information collected would be anecdotal, but still
included in the annual report.

Planning Manager Naughton explained how the use of SB2 grant funds for this project would
tackle both long and short range planning efforts, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.
She further explained the City’s goals in making the building of ADUs as easy and affordable
as possible for homeowners.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN highlighted the importance of maintaining local control and
land use, and noted this is a positive way to maintain local control.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN noted that many residents are worried about ADUs in their
neighbor’s backyards. He also noted that plumbing should be added to the Task 2 construction
documents when meeting with Michael Baker International.

Planning Manager Naughton and City Attorney Davis explained that the City could not be more
restrictive in ADU requirements than the current building code, in response to MAYOR PRO
TEM ZUCKERMAN. City Attorney Davis also explained that the State has made the building
of ADUs relatively easy and accessible, and that staff’s efforts are to gain control by providing
quality preapproved plans that will fit the character of the City.

Planning Manager Naughton explained the parking allowance that is outlined in the City’s
approved ADU ordinance, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR SCHMITZ commended staff for their work on the grant application and the efforts to
preserve the character of the City.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 10, 2020
 Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE TASK ORDER #4 - PROPOSAL FROM MBI TO PROVIDE
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN ADU
  PROGRAM, AS PART OF THE SB 2 PGP-AWARDED PROJECTS, IN A NOT-
  TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $69,982.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

D.  PROPOSITION 68 STATEWIDE PARK DEVELOPMENT AND COMMUNITY
  REVITALIZATION PROGRAM GRANT APPLICATION

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that it is not required under the grant to
allocate this money to George F Canyon, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho explained that this grant can supplement other
grants if needed towards this project, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN noted that the funds could also be used for environmental
protection, restoration project, water infrastructure, flood protection projects etc., and asked if
these other options were considered by staff. City Manager Grammer explained why staff felt
that George F Canyon was the best use for these grant funds.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2470 AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO
  SUBMIT AN APPLICATION FOR THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF
  PARKS AND RECREATION’S OFFICE OF GRANTS AND LOCAL SERVICES
  (OGALS) PROPOSITION 68 PER CAPITA PROGRAM AND EXECUTE ANY
  AGREEMENTS NECESSARY FOR THE USE OF GRANT FUNDS TOWARD
  THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER NEW DEVELOPMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
noting that LA County is reporting a spike in the number of daily cases, and remains in Tier 1
of the State’s 4-Tier reopening plan. The number of positive cases in RHE has remained fairly
stable with a total of 53 positive cases reported since March.

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided the following updates regarding
upcoming City Events:
  • The fall drive-in Movie Night on October 30 was a success with over 40 cars in
  attendance.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 10, 2020
   •  Registration opened Friday, October 30 for the Holiday House Decorating Contest,
  which will be judged the week of December 7.
  •  The Mayor’s Breakfast Ride will take place November 14 - 22, involving a trail riding
  experience highlighting certain equestrian points of interest within the City and a video
  featuring the Mayor at each location.
  •  The drive-thru Holiday Parade of Lights will be held on December 5 from 6:00 pm -
  10:00 pm at Ernie Howlett Park involving a collection of lit up holiday light displays.
  •  December 19 will be the third drive-in Movie Night at Ernie Howlett Park featuring the
  movie “Elf.”

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported on her first meeting on Southern California Association
of Government’s (SCAG) Energy and Environment Policy Committee.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also attended the South Bay Cities Council of Government’s
(SBCCOG) Steering Committee meeting this month.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that on November 17, the SBCCOG will be hosting
a Zoom celebration of the South Bay Fiber Network connection, and on November 19 the
SBCCOG Board of Director’s meeting will be held to honor retiring former SBCCOG Board
Chairs including COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN attended various SCAG subcommittee meetings this
month.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN also reported that California Contract Cities Association
(CCCA) will be hosting a City Manager’s virtual summit on November 19.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN expressed his excitement for the Holiday Parade of Lights
on December 5.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on the monthly Peninsula Mayor’s meeting with Southern
California Edison this month.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also reported on the successful “KICK-ASH Town Hall” hosted by
Peninsula High School students.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:52 P.M. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting in honor of Veterans
Day and all of those who have served and sacrificed for our country. The meeting was
adjourned to the next regular City Council meeting on Tuesday, November 24, 2020 at 7:00
pm for the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Velveth Schmitz
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 10, 2020
